title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Auth, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's controls, workflows, and operational guidance for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging practices and retention, data residency and retention requirements, secure SDLC controls, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence packaging, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for engineers, security reviewers, product owners, and compliance auditors.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: All production-facing control plane and runtime services, identity providers (IdP), audit pipelines, storage systems that hold customer data, and developer workflows that impact security posture.
- Audience: Security team, SRE, infra, eng-platform, product security reviewers, compliance owners, and auditors.

Principles:
- Least privilege by default.
- All admin actions are scoped and logged.
- Separation of duties for access and approval of sensitive changes.
- Evidence-first: controls must be demonstrable with reproducible artifacts.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Overview:
- Production console and APIs use role-based access control (RBAC) backed by our IdP (Okta) with SCIM provisioning. Service-to-service auth uses short-lived mTLS tokens (internal CA) and AAD-like role assertions for external customers.

Roles and role model (canonical):
- System Admin: full access to infra, billing, and security controls (limited to 3 people in prod).
- Platform Engineer: manage infra and platform services; no billing or PII export rights.
- SRE Oncall: limited runbook execution permissions (restart/scale) for incidents.
- Product Owner: product config and feature flags for their product area (no infra changes).
- ReadOnly: view-only for dashboards and logs.
- Service Account: machine identities scoped to a single service and set with expiration and approval policy.

Key controls and enforcement:
- Provisioning: SCIM-enabled groups in Okta synchronized to Redwood RBAC groups. Changes must go through HR / onboarding/offboarding flows (SCIM deprovisioning within 1 hour of termination ticket).
- MFA: Mandatory for all human accounts (Okta Verify or YubiKey).
- Session length: Interactive sessions expire after 8 hours for high-privilege roles, 24 hours for non-privileged roles.
- Access reviews: Quarterly automated access review for all groups with owners listed.
- Service account keys: Rotation policy: keys expire in 90 days; short-lived token pattern preferred (recommended use of Vault-issued tokens).

Implementation examples:
- CLI (Okta + Redwood RBAC):
  redwood auth login --idp okta --scope platform-engineer
- Terraform snippet (example role binding):
  provider "redwood" { }
  resource "redwood_rbac_binding" "platform_eng" {
    role = "platform_engineer"
    group = "okta:engineering-platform"
  }

Ownership and SLAs:
- RBAC service owner: eng-platform (owner: Marcus Jensen).
- IdP configuration owner: security (owner: Aisha Patel).
- SCIM sync SLA: 99.9% daily sync success; incidents escalate to eng-platform oncall.

2) Audit logging
What we log:
- Authentication events: successful and failed logins, MFA events, token issuance and revocation.
- Authorization changes: role/grant creation, modification, deletion, policy changes.
- Administrative operations: schema migrations, cluster reboots, deployment rollouts by user.
- Data exports and downloads: any export of customer data or PII.
- Service-to-service critical errors and rebuilds when they require manual approval.

Log pipeline and storage:
- Source collection: application and infra logs forwarded to Fluent Bit -> Kafka -> Splunk + cold-storage S3 (encrypted).
- Immutable retention: audit logs are written to append-only S3 with object-level immutability markers for enterprise customers who request compliance retention.
- Access: Logs are accessible via the Splunk console with RBAC. Direct S3 access is restricted to security and compliance engineers via session-based approvals.

Retention policy (default tiers):
- Auth & authorization audit logs: default 1 year.
- High-sensitivity audit logs (enterprise regulated customers): up to 7 years (configurable with contract).
- Operational logs (metrics, debug): 90 days.
- Evidence bundles exported for audits are versioned and retained per contract terms.

Alerting and detection thresholds (examples):
- 5 failed admin console logins within 10 minutes -> create high-severity alert in PagerDuty and create SOC ticket.
- Unusual data export (single export >1GB or >100k records) -> automatic hold and manual review by Data Protection Officer.

3) Data residency & retention
Data residency model:
- Customer data paths are tagged with region metadata at ingestion. Default storage region follows customer selection at provisioning.
- Cross-region backups are disabled by default; enabled only with explicit customer consent and contract.

Retention configuration options:
- Default tenant retention: 90 days for application data unless customer requests different SLA.
- Audit and compliance retention: configurable per contract (90 days, 1 year, 3 years, 7 years).

Requirements checklist for new region or on-prem deployment:
- Local KMS/HSM integration with customer key policies.
- Legal review for data export controls and cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs, BCRs).
- Localized logging and evidence collection pipeline.

Example table (as text) for typical retention defaults:
- Auth logs: 1 year
- Application logs: 90 days
- Backups (non-PII): 180 days
- Audit evidence (contractual): 7 years (where required)

4) Secure SDLC (secure software development lifecycle)
Controls (required for all services):
- Pull request requirement: All changes must be code-reviewed by at least two engineers, one from security or an appointed peer reviewer for security-sensitive code.
- Static Analysis: SAST runs on every PR (tool: Snyk/CodeQL).
- Dependency scanning: Dependabot/GitHub Dependabot alerts auto-create tickets; medium+ vulnerabilities block merge until triaged.
- IaC scanning: Terraform/CloudFormation plans scanned by Checkov or tfsec in CI.
- Secrets scanning: Pre-commit hooks and runtime secret detection; any detected secret triggers rotation and audit.
- CI gating: Unit tests, integration smoke, and performance smoke for runtime-affecting PRs.
- Release checklist: security sign-off, infra migration plan, rollback plan, SLO impact analysis.

Release & deployment controls:
- Canary rollouts for runtime binaries with canary evaluation metrics (latency, error rate, cost delta).
- Auto-fallback policies that revert to previous model variant on quality regressions.

Vulnerability management:
- SLA for critical CVEs: patch or mitigation in 72 hours.
- Moderates: 7 days.
- Low: tracked in backlog and reviewed every sprint.

5) Incident response (security procedures)
High-level incident flow:
1. Detection & Triage: Security/SRE receives alert via monitoring or third-party report.
2. Classification: Determine it as Security incident (S1-S4) using classification matrix.
3. Containment: Apply targeted containment actions (rotate keys, revoke sessions, isolate nodes).
4. Forensics & Evidence Collection: Preserve logs, snapshot disks, collect process memory if required.
5. Remediation: Patch, configuration change, or data recovery.
6. Communication: Notify stakeholders, customers (if required by policy), and regulators per SLA.
7. Postmortem: Publish blameless postmortem with timeline, root cause, fixes, and follow-ups.

Runbook excerpts (short checklist):
- On paging: Acknowledge within 15 minutes for high-severity incidents; join incident bridge within 30 minutes.
- Short-term containment steps:
  - Revoke admin sessions (Okta API): curl -X POST https://okta.example.com/api/v1/users/{id}/lifecycle/expire_session -H "Authorization: SSWS ${TOKEN}"
  - Rotate service account credentials via Vault: vault write auth/approle/role/rw-role/secret-id -force
- Evidence collection commands (examples):
  - Collect systemd journal for host: journalctl -u redwood-service --since "2026-05-20T00:00:00Z" > /out/host-journal.log
  - Export relevant Splunk query to JSON: splunk search "index=audit action=auth" -earliest @d -latest now -output json > /out/auth-audit.json

Notification & regulatory timelines:
- Customer-impacting data exposure: notify affected customers within 72 hours of confirmed breach per contract; escalate to legal & compliance immediately.
- Regulatory reporting: PII breach reporting timelines are jurisdiction-specific — legal must be consulted within 24 hours of confirmation.

6) Compliance evidence workflows
Evidence catalogue and owner model:
- Controls map: Each control has a control id, owner, evidence type, and retention. Example: CTRL-AUTH-01 -> owner: security -> evidence: Okta audit export, retention: 3 years.
- Evidence collector: automated job that assembles artifacts for an audit window (configurable dates) and packages them as signed bundles.

Audit packaging process (procedure):
1. Create evidence request ticket with scope and date range.
2. Security triggers automated evidence collector (runs on ephemeral host).
3. Collector exports logs, role bindings, provisioning history, change tickets, deployment manifests, and screenshots of console state where required.
4. Package is signed with security code-signing key and uploaded to compliance S3 bucket with ACL for auditors.
5. Delivery: provide download link and short integrity report to auditors.

Example artifacts included:
- Okta SCIM logs for the selected timeframe.
- Splunk saved search exports for authorization changes.
- GitHub PRs and merge commits for the release window (signed).
- Terraform state and plan artifacts for changes.

7) Risk & exceptions process
When an exception is required:
- Submit an Exception Request (template fields: control id, justification, compensating controls, expiration date, business owner, risk owner).
- Security assesses risk, recommends compensating controls, and assigns residual risk score.
- Approval matrix: Small scope exceptions (risk score <=10) can be approved by security lead; higher-scored exceptions require CISO approval and quarterly board review for >180 day exceptions.
- Expiry & review: All exceptions auto-expire at stated expiry; recurring exceptions must be renewed and re-approved.

Exception request example fields (as text):
- control_id: CTRL-IAC-03
- owner: eng-infra
- justification: temporary bypass for migration to new cloud provider
- compensating_controls: increased logging, time-limited IAM binding, extra monitoring
- requested_expiry: 2026-08-01

Metrics and reporting
- Quarterly compliance dashboard: percent of controls with evidence attached, number of active exceptions, mean time to remediate security findings.
- KPIs: 95% of high-impact audit evidence available within 48 hours of request; 0 open critical exceptions >72 hours without mitigation.
